preamble: Shift of the palatalized alveolar nasal [nʲ] to a true palatal (or alveolo-palatal) nasal [ɲ], moving the primary constriction from the alveolar ridge to the hard palate. In West Slavic, consonants softened before front vowels developed this way: Polish ń and Czech ň continue Common Slavic soft [nʲ], whereas Russian keeps a palatalized alveolar.

examples.from: Proto-Slavic *nebo 'sky' with soft [nʲ] before the front vowel (cf. Russian [ˈnʲebə])
examples.note: Polish soft n became the alveolo-palatal nasal spelled ń / ni.
In the main Czech depalatalization (13th–14th c.), softened consonants either merged with hard ones or became palatal ď, ť, ň; n before i became ň.
